summary.intent: Reduce complexity in the Callisto release tooling: split registry providers by ecosystem, slim workflow checks, simplify the JSON scanner, design `release --recover`, and check whether decision/intent/prepared-inputs types duplicate each other.
summary.outcome: Opened PRs #392, #393 and #395, wrote up the `release --recover` design, and completed the overlap review. Split `derive_release_commit_decision` into helpers (compiles, 19 decision tests pass, full CI run, PR shipped), and deferred the other cleanups.

repo: Decision, intent and prepared inputs are three deliberate layers: the decision is the committed roster (ADR 2), the intent is sealed by digest, and prepared operations hold private argv, paths and registry bindings.

`validate_intent` deliberately re-derives the intent and compares it with the received one. This is staleness detection and must run in `execute`, because the CI build and execute jobs are separate processes.
Callisto stays git-only (ADR 5), so the workflow must keep the GitHub-side checks (exactly one managed PR, GitHub-verified merge commit).
A candidate release that can never succeed (e.g. the E180 tag-push case) would block later releases, since releases are sequential. The escape is to fix it or pass `--from <sha>`.
`just bench` exists and is the stated gate for deciding whether to merge the repeated derivations.

code.finding: `derive_release_commit_decision` was about 234 lines doing four jobs: HEAD/parent verification, diff and path policy, decision decode and claim checks, batched manifest and changelog checks. It was split into helpers.
`derive_release_roster` (:198) and `releases_tagged_at` (:286) repeat the 'unreleased version' entry-building loop, and tag template rendering appears at :274 and :302.
Copies `git_remote` and `operations` from `PreparedDerivation` into `PreparedReleaseInputs`, so the two structs overlap.
`plan_release` derives once. Guards at :207, :296 and :331 can each derive again, and the CLI validation derives a further time (`release.rs:121`), giving up to 5 derivations on a real local release.
`release_package_ids` already unifies package id computation across 6 call sites.

workflow: Run the full CI after a refactor. The unit tests alone don't exercise the end-to-end release checks.
Set a benefit threshold for cleanups. Skip tidy-ups with no user-visible gain, and gate risky ones on measurement.
Teammate reports can arrive truncated, so ask for the remainder via SendMessage rather than acting on partial findings.
Reading-based call counts from a reviewer who ran no cargo builds are estimates, not measurements.

friction: The overlap report was truncated mid-finding 5 and needed a follow-up request.
The reviewer ran no cargo builds, so the derivation counts are unmeasured.
The end-to-end release tests that exercise the decision check run only in full CI, not locally.
open_items: Build `callisto release --recover`: the discovery function, `release pending --format json`, the action changes, the ADR 3 amendment and removal of ADR 13. First confirm the cost of observing old candidates and that committed-decision verification works at arbitrary commits.
Split `registry_argv.rs` (1,201 lines) by ecosystem as a follow-up, if wanted.
Deferred low-value cleanups: fold `PreparedDerivation` into `PreparedReleaseInputs`, merge the duplicate roster loops, and dedupe the tag rendering.
Share one derivation across the local guards in `plan_release` (medium risk because guard ordering changes). Do it only if `just bench` shows a cost.
Check `derive.rs` (about 1090 production lines) for further splits; the largest-function scan was only partial.
